extra.summary: 6061 plate replaced by a ribbed PA-CF saddle (6 mm skin + 6 mm ribs, x -92..-80) that is the wing's outboard end; 2 mm steel doubler (140x44) backs the 4 x M5 knurled brass inserts; armour keel feet re-seated on the saddle rear face.
extra.spec_basis: spec plate 278 g -> saddle 104 g + doubler 95 g (proxy volumes)
contract_changes: Plate part number removed: wing tongue seat, 4 x M5 base pattern, clasp-foot M4 pairs, keel M4 feet now land in/behind the saddle (inserts instead of tapped 6061); plate.json and chassis_axilla.py retired; wing/saddle become one print or a lap joint.
Clasp feet (front face) need M4 brass inserts in the saddle skin; skin must thicken to >=6 mm at those feet (done by 6 mm skin).
decision_conflicts: None of: no backplate, no hip belt, 270 deg clasp, 5 deg rule, ball-styled joints. Saddle outline equals the plate outline (158x100), so it is not a backplate. Rigid part sits at x >= -92, >= 26 mm off skin; nothing new on moving skin.
Touches 'plate 6061' choice made by Claude (not Forest).

calcs.name: load case
calcs.formula: W=(m_arm+m_stage) g; Mc=W*0.080 m; M_y=Mc+S2 cap
calcs.inputs: m_arm 1.566 kg, m_stage 2.2 kg (assumed), cap 8.3 N.m

calcs.name: bolt group
calcs.formula: T_pair=M_y/p (p=26 mm z pitch), per bolt=T_pair/2; dynamic x2; shear=sqrt((8.3/0.124)^2+W^2)/4 N
calcs.result: per-bolt tension 216 N static, 433 N at x2; shear 19 N; conservative (ignores base-block bearing on the saddle face)

calcs.name: insert pull-out
calcs.inputs: ~1000 N typical for knurled brass in PA-CF (UNVERIFIED vendor figure)
calcs.result: SF 4.6 static, 2.3 at x2 (marginal at x2; doubler loads the inserts through the steel, so bench pull-test required)

calcs.name: saddle section
calcs.formula: I=sum(b h^3/12 + A d^2); sigma=M c/I
calcs.inputs: skin 158x6, 7 cross ribs 3x6, centroid 3.70 mm, c 8.30 mm, PA-CF flexural strength ~100 MPa (UNVERIFIED), y-running ribs ignored
calcs.result: I=7226 mm4, sigma=12.9 MPa -> SF 7.7 vs 100 MPa; mid-thickness assumed isotropic, layer lines across the 6 mm skin are the weak direction

extra.printability: Saddle 158x100x12: fits 256 cube; print skin flat on bed (rear face -80 down) so layers run in the plane of the skin; ribs up, no supports; bolt tension then acts across layers in the skin only through the steel doubler. Wing lap or one-piece print needs rotation (wing ~ 62x105 as proxy) - keep as lap joint.
pros: ~79 g lighter per arm than the 6061 plate (spec 278 g)
no waterjet/tap step; wing and plate one design, re-fit (I7) is a re-run
cons: load path now PA-CF across layers; inserts and doubler carry everything
loses the 6061 stiffness for the S2 8.3 N.m reaction
creep under sustained weight (PA-CF) not characterised
risks: PA-CF creep/anneal distortion of a 158x100 saddle
gates_to_rerun: body_loads (stall limit uses plate stiffness assumptions)
assumptions: proxy geometry, not the verified STLs
proxy basis overstates armour mass (REF armour 161.6 g vs spec 110.6 g)
